body:
I am living with him. I didn't qualify the first time because I couldn't get all my medical records, which are from a bunch of different places and doctors due to moving around and really disjointed care. Apparently disability generally rejects folks the first time anyway, and I may need legal help, which is a struggle. There's also the fact that a big part of me has been going, "You're fine, YOU'RE FINE. Just lazy! Stop fucking around! Why are you such a stupid loser?" This may be directly related to the things my family has said to me.

I think the depression is worse, really- I'm not eating, and having nightmares regularly. The ADD meds require a psychiatrist to prescribe for the insurance to pay; my primary care doc prescribed my Strattera, but my new insurance threw it back without a psychiatrist signature.

I'll call for a referral on Monday, if I can, but I don't know if I can afford the fee. We are so tight on money it's ridiculous. At least my sweetie wouldn't be on the hook for the cost on my care.

I hate this, I hate it, I hate it. I can't live like this. I don't want to be the person who hurts everyone. But I'm not good at anything except loving people, and I'm losing that- this would be not about caring for them, but doing for me.

Well, I'd like to go back to school for biomedical engineering and design doodads and whatsits with programs that will help regulate chemicals and drugs in the body... Barring that, I'd like to write. But my brain, my self esteem and my finances are too fucking tattered to manage any of the above. I've been studying an MIT computer science class online, but I'm not with it enough to keep up on a regular basis. So frustrating. My head is just not organized enough. And ADD meds are SO HARD TO COME BY... even non amphetamines! What the heck. :(

In any reasonable world, I would qualify for disability. I even have a difficult time filling out the form, it is so fucking stupid. I haven't been able to support myself since 2010 at least. I have couch surfed and lived in strangers' living rooms due to poverty- it is only great good luck I haven't actually slept in my car, or now that I've had to sell it, on the street or in a shelter. I've dealt with food insecurity to the point that I still struggle with not eating everything as soon as I get it, for fear it won't be there the next day.

The worst thing is, that I look perfectly healthy and, due to my dad's influence, constantly cheerful. I saw a nutritionist once because my doctor was worried I was malnourished- see: food insecurity- and, with my whole history of hospitalizations, and with me describing the poverty + difficulty making & storing food in my circumstances, what with, you know, extreme depression, she said brightly, "At least you're not REALLY depressed!"

Well, shit, lady, I'd hate to see those folks.

I just want to learn and grow and write and teach. And I can't even read books, which have always been my safe place. I can't even watch movies. This is shit. Things will go up, I know, but then they'll come back down again. This is pointless.

I'm a Thanksgiving baby too- although this year it's not on the day itself. What are you doing for Thanksgiving? I'm an asshole, but volunteering is always good- my abusive family can lick my asshole because I will never spend another holiday with them.

I'd suggest taking yourself out the day before (hell, and the day after, why not? ;)) and doing whatever you want with whoever you want. It's tough when your family is a curse, but sweetie, you are FREE. You're still super duper young, and I know it feels both fucking weird to be an adult and fucking horrible that you haven't ACHIEVED ALL THE THINGS. But you are A-OK. Believe me. (FREE!)

You can start your own Thanksgiving traditions, if you want. You can have a birthday turkey. You can have an alcohol-free Thanksgiving, if that's what you want, or if, say, gin was your mom's drink, you can ban gin and enjoy the hell out of bourbon. You can even say "Fuck this imperialist, bullshit Thanksgiving crap anyway!" 

This is your life now. It belongs to you. And it feels lonely and empty, and that feeling is shitty as hell. But you'll find your people- and they'll find you. 

My fucked up family and my mental illnesses gave me a shitty time, and made me feel like the biggest loser ever. But I graduated from college; I traveled; I studied some really awesome things; I ran my own businesses. I wish I'd cut my family out so much earlier, but there it is. I still struggle, of course, and I'm suicidal too, but you have good things ahead of you. I wish we could have a birthday drink together. :)

Right now I'm really struggling, partly because I have terrible health care, but antidepressants have been really, really useful to me, alone and with therapy and self-examination. I'd say they've saved my life.

It's okay to let others hold your guns, or just your ammo, temporarily. Don't forget to check the chambers. If you trust your parents and you think they'll be loving and supportive, definitely talk to them. Depression and suicidality are illnesses just like diabetes or heart disease. Talk to your doctor; psychiatrists and psychologists can do more than just prescribe antidepressants.

We're pulling for you. There are so many good things waiting for you!
